lessons.culture: The adhan calls people to each of the five daily prayers, and the iqamah, said just before the prayer starts, tells everyone to stand in rows; in the Gulf the iqamah comes a few minutes after the adhan, and many masjids show the times on a board or screen. Men and women usually have separate entrances and prayer areas. Someone who joins late prays with the imam, then stands and completes the missed rak'ahs after the imam's salaam. The prayer names, the adhan and the iqamah are fixed wording shared by all Arabic dialects.

lessons.culture: Wudu is the washing done before prayer, and masjids keep a wudu area, usually near the toilets, with taps and seats. Gulf masjids are carpeted, so shoes come off at the door and go on a rack; clothes should be clean and modest, and phones are put on silent so nobody's prayer is disturbed. The qibla is the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah.

lessons.culture: Jumu'ah replaces the Dhuhr prayer on Friday and is prayed in congregation after a khutbah. Many people bathe, wear clean clothes and come early, and during the khutbah everyone listens in silence. In a crowded masjid the rows are filled by moving closer together, and after the prayer people greet each other with جُمُعَةٌ مُبَارَكَة and تَقَبَّلَ اللَّهُ مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ.

lessons.culture: Many masjids in the Gulf run Qur'an circles (7alagaat) for adults and children, often after Maghrib or Asr, where each student recites to the teacher, who is addressed as أستاذ or شيخ. The mushaf is handled with respect: held with clean hands, kept off the floor and returned to its shelf after use. The blessings and the Qur'an words said here are fixed wording shared by all dialects.

challenge.title: A Visit to the Masjid
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines at the masjid. Ask which prayer is next and when the iqamah is, find the wudu area, the shoe rack and the qibla, answer a polite request about your phone, find the entrance, and say what you do when you are late. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 17 and keep the fixed religious wording exact.
required_elements: A question about the next prayer or the time of the adhan or iqamah, with شنو or متى.
A question about the entrance or the wudu area, with وين.
A request for, or a mention of, the shoe rack, the prayer rug or the qibla.
A polite request or reply about the phone with لو سمحت or مشكور.
A missed rak'ah explained with فاتتني and a closing تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ with its reply مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ.
